chunks: From him, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:

I asked him about a man who is behind the Imam, and the Imam prolongs the Tashahhud, so the man feels the urge to urinate, or fears that something will be missed, or a pain befalls him. How should he act? He said: 'He should recite the Tashahhud, turn around (to face the Imam), and leave the Imam (praying alone).'

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدَ: The sitting portion of the prayer where testimonies are recited
key_terms.يَنْصَرِفُ: He turns around / concludes his prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a worshipper do if the Imam prolongs the Tashahhud and he needs to relieve himself or has pain?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the principle of *rukun* (pillar) versus *sunnah* in congregational prayer, allowing the follower to break the unity of prayer when necessity (*darurah*) arises. Notably, the worshipper recites the Tashahhud independently before turning to the Imam, a nuance that distinguishes this specific scenario from general rulings on breaking prayer. It underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on balancing ritual perfection with practical ease (*rukhsah*) during prolonged standing or sitting.
